A much drier regime has moved in over the Marianas this afternoon. 
However, the monsoon pattern still supports the development of 
scattered showers across the region later this evening near midnight.
Latest model guidance indicates a drier pattern than previously 
expected. This has resulted in decreased POPs (Probability of 
Precipitation) over the next several days. Periods of locally heavy 
showers, along with gusty winds in heavier showers, remain a 
possibility through Sunday, though it does now look less likely. 

Marine/Surf...
Not much going on in the marine environment over the next few days.
Benign seas and light to gentle winds will persist through Tuesday.
Seas will maintain a moderate risk of rip currents along west and
north facing reefs. Next week, seas will begin to build early in the
week, reaching up to 8 feet by Thursday. This could bring the rip
current risk to moderate along east facing reefs and possibly high 
along west facing reefs. Winds will become occasionally moderate 
around the middle of next week.

Tropical Systems...
As of earlier this afternoon, Typhoon Bang-lang (20W) was located 
near 23N168E rapidly moving north-northeast at 22 mph. Maximum
sustained winds remain at 75 mph and is forecasted to intensify
through tonight. Bang-lang's wind field remains compact, with 
typhoon-force winds extending outward from the center up to 10 
miles and tropical storm-force winds up to 50 miles. It is expected 
to make a slight turn toward the north with little change in forward 
speed through Sunday. This general forecast track will continue 
taking Bang-lang away from Wake Island, passing north of 25N and out 
of our region possibly later tonight or early Sunday morning.

For more information on TY Bang-lang, please see bulletins issued by
the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN33 PGTW and 
by the National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ33 PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
Satellite imagery depicts mostly cloudy skies and scattered showers 
across all three forecast points. Scatterometry indicates gentle to
moderate winds across Pohnpei, and light to gentle winds over Kosrae
and Majuro. An active phase of the monsoon trough is forecasted 
through the weekend, moreso concentrated over Pohnpei as the trough
shifts westward over the next few days. Heavier showers with 
convective gusts are most likely for Pohnpei, so a headline and 
additional wording was included through Sunday night. Kosrae is 
currently in a drier slot, but outflow boundaries upstream and 
cooling cloud tops just to the north warranted high-end scattered 
showers and isolated thunderstorms for tonight, peaking to numerous 
on Sunday, before decreasing through the rest of the week. As for 
Majuro, diffusive flow will continue over the atolls, maintaining 
light to gentle winds, but showers will remain scattered with 
isolated thunderstorms possible through the weekend. Then, there is 
potential for drier weather across the entire region, with isolated 
showers forecasted during the work week.

Altimetry and buoy data indicates combined seas of 4 to 6 ft across 
the region with primary swell directions out of the west, south, and
east at Pohnpei, Kosrae, and Majuro, respectively. At Pohnpei, those
with marine interests should consider the elevated winds with 
convective moderate gusts through the weekend. At this time, sea 
conditions are not expected to be hazardous to small craft, but this 
could change depending on the intensity and duration of the monsoon 
trough.

Western Micronesia...
Satellite imagery shows scattered showers across Chuuk and isolated 
showers across Palau and Yap. Altimetry shows combined seas are 
between 3 and 6 feet across the region. 

The forecast remains status quo for Palau. Dry conditions look to 
prevail through the period and beyond. Drought concerns are growing 
as the favorable rain pattern remains north of Palau. For now, 
isolated light showers remain in the forecast with satellite still 
showing weak squalls moving across the region. PWAT values are 
generally between 1.5 inches and 1.75 inches, so accumulations from 
these showers are expected to be below the 0.20 inches wetting rain 
threshold. 

Yap will begin the period equally as dry as Palau. PWATS have fallen 
below 2.00 inches over the last day and drier air will continue to 
mix in from the southwest. This brief dry stretch will come to an end 
by Monday as the monsoon pattern looks to re-orient itself. High-end 
(50%) scattered showers will be possible Monday through Tuesday 
night before a slight decrease in shower coverage to 40% is 
possible. Conditions look to dry out once again beyond Thursday next 
week. 

A difficult forecast is in store for Chuuk through the weekend. 
Guidance continues to hit them hard with showers and thunderstorms 
over the next 36 to 48 hours. A weak tropical disturbance is
